Why is my scrolling banner slowly moving upwards? [NSFW]

In your CSS stylesheet you specified:

/* Header animation */
@keyframes header-anim{
 0%{
 background-position:0 0;
 }
 
 100%{
 background-position:2249px 22px;
 }
}

@-webkit-keyframes header-anim{
 0%{
 background-position:0 0;
 }
 
 100%{
 background-position:2249px 22px;
 }
}

0% being the first keyframe (like in animation) and 100% being the last. Your last keyframe puts the background-position at an X of 2249px and a Y of 22px. That means that slowly but surely it will go up/down. If you don't want it do go up/down, you should keep the Y at 0. So 100% should be background-position:2249px 0px;.

What ever could tout be referring to? There are no insane white supremacists here!

That quote is attributed to Einstein, and it's wrong.

First of all, insanity is a legal term. I think Albert E worked in a patent office before getting all famous, but that doesn't give him the authority to define how things should work in a criminal court. Second, even if it was a psychological term, Einstein wasn't a psychologist, and as such, his definition of insanity is really no better than anyone else's.

Third, the fact of the matter is that doing the same thing over and over again is not only normal and natural, but necessary. People can't be conditioned by a single stimulus, and also don't have access to perfect information - let alone the ability to process it instantaneously. Sometimes, doing (what appears to be) the same thing repeatedly can in fact yield different results, particularly if people can't identify which phenomena are results of the done-thing. I might walk the same hiking trail once a month, but that doesn't mean I'll twist my ankle every time I do so, even though twisting my ankle was a result of me going for a hike.

Sure, it's good to be able to find an underlying principle beneath the results (i.e. my dexterity improves as I take more hikes.) But that takes time and brainpower that could instead be spent thinking about butts, which is something our brains are much better at.
